item.title: She Tried To Kill Him. Then She Cross-Examined Him
item.description: Sheila Davalloo’s husband survived her 2003 attack during a blindfolded guessing game. Years later, she represented herself and questioned him at her trial for killing romantic rival Anna Lisa Raymundo. Her convictions brought consecutive prison sentences totaling 75 years.

item.title: Her Missing Skull Was Found In David Attenborough’s Garden
item.description: Maid Kate Webster was convicted and executed for murdering Julia Martha Thomas in Richmond in 1879. In 2010, builders discovered a skull in David Attenborough’s garden. A coroner identified it as Thomas’s the following year, resolving a mystery spanning more than a century.

item.title: The Gun Hidden Inside A Medical Student’s Textbook
item.description: Investigators found the gun linked to Julissa Brisman’s 2009 killing inside medical student Philip Markoff’s hollowed-out textbook. He pleaded not guilty and died before trial. Gambling debts were investigated, but his motive was never conclusively established.

item.title: Reported For Abuse, His Counselor Returned With A Gun
item.description: Ohio social worker Payton Shires sexually abused a 13-year-old boy she was counseling. After his mother contacted police, Shires appeared at their home armed and threatened her. She pleaded guilty to abuse, intimidation and inducing panic, receiving four years and nine months in prison in 2024.

item.title: A Reporter Texted Her Phone. Her Killer Replied.
item.description: Carol Maltesi, known as Charlotte Angie, was murdered near Milan in January 2022. When a reporter contacted her phone, Davide Fontana replied pretending to be her. His refusal to send a voice message raised suspicions. An appeals court sentenced him to life in September 2026.

item.title: Her Mother Kept Her In A Wheelchair She Didn’t Need
item.description: Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s mother fabricated serious illnesses and forced her to use a wheelchair. In 2015, Gypsy helped plan her mother’s murder with boyfriend Nicholas Godejohn. She pleaded guilty to second-degree murder, received a 10-year sentence and completed parole in June 2025.

item.title: He Filed For Divorce. She Killed Their Two Children.
item.description: In November 2016, Brandi Worley killed Tyler, 7, and Charlee, 3, at their Indiana home a day after her husband filed for divorce. She admitted the killings in a 911 call and told police she feared losing the children. She pleaded guilty to two murders and received 120 years in prison in 2018.

item.title: He Left Her For Dead. She Testified Against Him Twice.
item.description: Mary Vincent, 15, survived Lawrence Singleton’s attack after accepting a ride in California in 1978. Her testimony helped convict him. After his release and the murder of Roxanne Hayes, Vincent testified again at his 1998 penalty hearing. He was sentenced to death.
